delete_intro_pairs.item: The user prefers engineering-style technical specifications with API endpoints and data schemas in campaign briefs instead of audience personas and brand voice.
The user prefers informational promotional email paragraphs with no calls to action, urgency language, or conversion-focused hooks.
The user prefers passive voice and neutral corporate tone in social media captions with no hashtags, hooks, or platform-native engagement patterns.
The user always prioritizes cities hosting music festivals and nightlife for industry conference travel over relevant sessions and networking.
The user always commits the entire campaign budget to a single channel with no testing, A/B splits, or cross-channel coordination.
The user always picks marketing channels with no attribution or analytics capability and ignores ROI measurement.
The user prefers academic citation style with footnotes and theoretical references in brand voice guidelines instead of practical examples.
The user always chooses the broadest possible ad audience with no segmentation, lookalikes, or exclusion lists.
The user prefers extremely long background narratives over 800 words in press releases with minimal news hook or quotable executive statements.
The user always chooses the cheapest stock footage and generic templates for campaign creative over custom shoots or brand-specific assets.
